title: The H–R Diagram
objective: After this level you can read the basic pattern of the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram.
summary: Plot stars by luminosity and temperature and a pattern appears: the main sequence, with giants above and white dwarfs below.

cards.headline: Put every star on one chart and a hidden pattern jumps out.
Luminosity versus temperature
cards.body: The Hertzsprung–Russell diagram plots stars by how luminous they are and how hot their surfaces are. It’s named after Ejnar Hertzsprung and Henry Norris Russell, who developed it independently in the early 1900s.

cards.headline: Where the stars fall
cards.body: Most stars fall along a diagonal band called the main sequence. The Sun sits near its middle, though most stars are dimmer red dwarfs. Red giants sit in the upper right: cool but very luminous. White dwarfs sit in the lower left: hot but dim. A star’s place on the chart tells you what stage of life it’s in.

cards.headline: H–R diagram: read
learned: The H–R diagram plots luminosity against temperature
Most stars lie on the main sequence
Red giants: upper right; white dwarfs: lower left
A star’s position shows its life stage

questions.prompt: What two properties does the H–R diagram plot?

options.label: Distance and age
options.rationale: Neither axis is distance or age.

options.label: Size and color only
options.rationale: The axes are luminosity and temperature.

questions.explanation: The H–R diagram plots each star’s luminosity against its surface temperature.

questions.prompt: Where on the H–R diagram are white dwarfs found?

options.label: In the middle of the main sequence
options.rationale: The Sun is there, not white dwarfs.

options.label: Upper left: hot and very bright

questions.explanation: White dwarfs are hot but small, so they’re dim: lower left on the diagram.

questions.prompt: From Level 9: a blue-white star is hotter than a red one. On the H–R diagram, which side is it on?

options.label: The right side, with cooler stars
options.rationale: Hotter stars are on the left.

options.label: The left side, with hotter stars
The bottom, with the dimmest stars
options.rationale: Color tells temperature, which is left–right.

options.label: It isn’t on the diagram
options.rationale: All kinds of stars can be plotted.

questions.explanation: Temperature runs left to right on the H–R diagram, hottest on the left, so a blue-white star sits to the left of a red one.
